clue.text: Maybe bitter about support having one form of vitamin deficiency

indicators.note: to be about something is to surround it, so one word wraps around the other

blocks.note: bitter is one kind of beer, hence 'maybe'
a rib is a supporting member, as in a boat or vault
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A pub drinker whose diet of ale has left them short of vitamins.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter is a British pale ale, so beer is the container; the support goes inside it before the one is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Beriberi is a disease caused by lack of thiamine, one of the B vitamins.

clue.text: Seed-cases almost split

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: to split open is to burst

explanation.surface: Seed pods that have nearly broken open.
explanation.definitionFit: Burs are prickly seed heads or husks that cling to clothing and fur.

clue.text: Look enviously as Yankees ace bats

indicators.note: bats is slang for crazy, so the letters before it go mad and rearrange

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Rivals glare jealously as the New York Yankees' star pitcher takes his turn at the plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bats' looks like a baseball verb for the ace, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye askance is to regard someone with suspicion or envy, looking at them sideways.

clue.text: Get remote back, mischievous child overturned jumble

indicators.note: going back means reading the word from its end to its start
something overturned is upside down, which in a down clue means read backwards

blocks.note: remote means far away
an elf is a small mischievous creature, used of an impish child

explanation.surface: A frustrated parent snatches back the TV remote after an imp knocked over a pile of jumble.
explanation.walkthrough: Each piece is turned round separately. Jumble here is a noun meaning rubbish, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers gives raffle as an old word for rubbish or lumber, the sort of mixed junk collected at a jumble sale.

clue.text: As before, did suit one in smartest clothing

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another, here within the clothing word

blocks.note: your Sunday best is your smartest clothing
a means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: Someone in their finest outfit once made a suit look good.
explanation.walkthrough: BES(A)T. 'As before' marks the definition as an archaic usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Besit is an old verb meaning to fit or become, and besat is its past tense.

clue.text: Giants of yore seen wandering round Troy

indicators.note: wandering letters stray from their places and settle in a new order
going round something means surrounding it, so the shuffled letters enclose another

blocks.note: taken as written
t is the abbreviation for troy weight

explanation.surface: Legendary giants spotted roaming around the walls of ancient Troy.
explanation.walkthrough: Troy is not the city but troy weight, abbreviated t.
explanation.definitionFit: Eten or ettin is an old word for a giant from folklore, so etens are giants of former times.

clue.text: Naughty lady whipping out a pair in a flash

indicators.note: naughty means misbehaving, so the letters will not stay in line
whipping something out is removing it quickly, so a letter is taken away

blocks.note: taken as written
the letter to be removed
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cheeky woman flashing a pair of something in an instant.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the A out of lady and mix what remains with pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done in a flash happens very quickly, which is what the adverb rapidly means.

clue.text: Witch close to reaching broken ground in moss

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its last letter is kept

blocks.note: a hag is an ugly old witch
the final letter of reaching

explanation.surface: A witch nearly arriving at a patch of rough boggy land.
explanation.walkthrough: Moss here is the Scots word for a bog or peat moor.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots and northern dialect a hagg is a hole or broken patch in a peat bog.

clue.text: Pragmatist condemned US hitman

indicators.note: something condemned is wrecked or ruined, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A hard-headed realist denounces an American contract killer.
explanation.definitionFit: Humanism was the name F.C.S. Schiller gave to his version of pragmatist philosophy, so a humanist in that sense is a pragmatist.

clue.text: Fighter at peak grabbed by scalp in offensive

indicators.note: grabbed by means held inside, so the answer sits within the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: A soldier on a summit seized by the scalp during an attack.
explanation.walkthrough: Offensive is a military push, so the war picture hides the letters in plain sight.
explanation.definitionFit: An alpino is an Italian mountain soldier, a fighter trained for high peaks.

clue.text: Mushrooms, vegetables packing a bit of texture

indicators.note: packing means stuffing something inside, so the vegetables hold the rest
a small bit of a word is just its opening letter

blocks.note: greens are green vegetables
taken as written
the opening letter of texture

explanation.surface: A recipe of fungi and veg with a little added texture.
explanation.walkthrough: Mushrooms is a verb here, not the fungi: GRE(AT)ENS.
explanation.definitionFit: To mushroom is to grow quickly in size, and greatens means increases or enlarges.

clue.text: Crack near flattened structure reduced radius of bone cavity

blocks.note: a crack shot is an ace, an expert
in anatomy a tabula is a flat plate or flattened structure
radius shortened to its abbreviation, r

explanation.surface: An anatomy note about a fracture near a flattened bone.
explanation.walkthrough: Crack is not a fracture but an expert; radius is the geometric abbreviation, not the arm bone.
explanation.definitionFit: The acetabulum is the socket in the hip bone, and acetabular is its adjective.

clue.text: Recycle boxes following raffle

indicators.note: to box something is to enclose it, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: to recycle something is to reuse it
f is the standard abbreviation for following

explanation.surface: Collecting boxes for recycling after a charity raffle.
explanation.walkthrough: RE(F)USE. Raffle is the old word for rubbish, as at 3 down, not a prize draw.
explanation.definitionFit: Raffle is an archaic term for rubbish or lumber, so it means the same as refuse.

clue.text: Large lantern left to the end, it closes sale

indicators.note: the left, abbreviated l, is sent to the end of the word, rotating its letters
what closes a word is its final letter

blocks.note: a lantern is a kind of lamp
the final letter of sale

explanation.surface: A big lantern left until last, the item that ends the auction.
explanation.walkthrough: The L of lamp moves to the back to give AMPL, then the last letter of sale finishes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ample means plentiful or generously sized, a synonym for large.

clue.text: Newspaper article read out in short message

indicators.note: something read out is spoken aloud, so we go by how the words sound

blocks.note: a letterette is a short letter, a brief message

explanation.surface: An editorial read out as a brief message.
explanation.walkthrough: A letterette, a little letter, said with a soft T sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaderette is a short leading article or editorial in a newspaper.

clue.text: Dye spread through fabric after mostly careful wearing

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: a careful driver is a safe driver
colours that ran spread through the fabric
wearing a coat is being in it

explanation.surface: A colour that bled through the cloth after rather careless wear.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about laundry; the colour words are the definition and one piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Safranin is a red synthetic dye used in staining biological samples.

clue.text: Sacked partisan candidate

indicators.note: sacked can mean plundered and wrecked, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A party loyalist dismissed from standing for office.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspirant is someone seeking a position, such as a candidate for election.

clue.text: Old birds fancy ripe acai

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or fanciful, so the letters are rearranged decoratively

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Elderly people who like eating ripe acai berries.
explanation.walkthrough: Old birds sounds like slang for older women, but it is an old name for a group of real birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Picariae was a former taxonomic order of birds including woodpeckers and kingfishers, now abandoned.

clue.text: York’s good-for-nothing old grammar protecting name

indicators.note: protecting something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: a donat was an old grammar book, named after the Roman grammarian Donatus
n is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire layabout clings to an old grammar book to defend his name.
explanation.walkthrough: DON(N)AT. York's flags a Yorkshire dialect word.
explanation.definitionFit: In Yorkshire dialect a donnat is an idle, worthless person, a ne'er-do-well.

clue.text: Earth filling hides loose bundles of things

indicators.note: a filling goes inside something, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: animal hides are skins
E is the abbreviation for Earth

explanation.surface: Soil stuffed inside animal pelts that are tied together.
explanation.definitionFit: Skeins are loosely coiled lengths of yarn, or by extension tangled masses of things.

clue.text: Love is number one commitment

blocks.note: is shortened to 's, as in it's
number one is a child's word for a wee
a tie is a binding obligation or commitment

explanation.surface: A romantic saying that love comes before every other duty.
explanation.walkthrough: Number one is nursery slang for urinating, and wee is the British word for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Love and sweetie are both affectionate terms of address for a dear person.

clue.text: US Defense Dept taking in electronic semiconductor

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it inside, so a letter goes within

blocks.note: DoD is the US Department of Defense
in shortened to its initial
e is the standard prefix for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: The Pentagon acquiring electronic components.
explanation.walkthrough: D(I)OD then E: the department holds the I near its front, and E goes on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A diode is a semiconductor device that lets current flow in only one direction.

clue.text: Religious festival dance by church

blocks.note: a pas is a step or dance in ballet
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A festive dance held beside a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasch is an old name for the feast of Passover or of Easter.

clue.text: Woman adopting new son takes Charlie

indicators.note: adopting means taking someone in, so a letter is placed inside the woman

blocks.note: sort is Australian slang for a woman
n is the abbreviation for new
s is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A woman who takes in a newborn son and names him Charlie.
explanation.walkthrough: S(N)ORT plus S. Charlie is slang for cocaine, not a child's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To snort a drug is to inhale it through the nose, and Charlie is a slang term for cocaine.

clue.text: Sycophants longing to welcome business type

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a yen is a longing
an SME is a small or medium-sized enterprise

explanation.surface: Flatterers eager to greet a certain sort of company.
explanation.definitionFit: Yes-men agree with everything their superiors say, which is what sycophants do.

clue.text: Second rattling sound could be spirit

blocks.note: a mo is a moment or second
a rale is a rattling sound heard in diseased lungs

explanation.surface: A second rattle might be a ghost.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a haunting, but spirit means confidence here.
explanation.definitionFit: Morale is the confidence and enthusiasm of a group, often called its team spirit.

clue.text: Hotel took in native

blocks.note: an inn is a small hotel
to take in food is to eat it

explanation.surface: A hotel welcomed a local.
explanation.walkthrough: Took in looks like an insertion signal, but it simply means consumed.
explanation.definitionFit: Native and innate both describe qualities someone is born with rather than acquires.

clue.text: Seabird rarely seen about low hill

blocks.note: ca is short for circa, about
a how is a low hill or burial mound in northern English place names

explanation.surface: A rare seabird spotted circling a small hill.
explanation.definitionFit: The cahow, or Bermuda petrel, was thought extinct for centuries and remains one of the rarest seabirds.

clue.text: Loose head in RU game quits

indicators.note: the head is cut loose, so the opening letter is detached and dropped

blocks.note: sevens is the seven-a-side form of rugby union

explanation.surface: A rugby loosehead prop walks out of a match.
explanation.walkthrough: Loose head is a front-row rugby position, but here it means lose the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To be quits is to be level with nobody owing anything, which is what evens means.

clue.text: Gathering round American very embarrassed with facial hair

indicators.note: going round means surrounding, so the gathering encloses the next letters

blocks.note: a bee is a social gathering, as in a sewing bee
A is short for American
v is the abbreviation for very
red-faced with embarrassment

explanation.surface: A blushing American at a party sporting a beard.
explanation.walkthrough: BE(AV)E then RED. A beaver is old slang for a beard.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaver was a slang term for a beard, so beavered means bearded.

clue.text: Valley? He drew it with line

blocks.note: del., for delineavit, is written on a drawing beside the artist's name
l is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: An artist sketches a valley with a single stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: A dell is a small wooded hollow or valley.

clue.text: Poet’s spiritual following leaving mystical land

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: f is the abbreviation for following
faerie is fairyland, the realm of enchantment

explanation.surface: A poet's religious followers abandon a magical kingdom.
explanation.walkthrough: Poet's flags a literary spelling, from Spenser.
explanation.definitionFit: In poetic usage aerie is a variant of airy, meaning ethereal or unworldly.

clue.text: Chief witch putting tail of mouse on tom?

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its last letter
putting one thing on another attaches it after, so the clue's first piece is placed second

blocks.note: a tom is a he-cat, a male cat
the final letter of mouse

explanation.surface: A head witch attaching a mouse tail to her tomcat.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark warns that tom is defined loosely, as a he-cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Hecate is the Greek goddess of witchcraft, and in Macbeth she is the queen of the witches.

clue.text: Fringes of occult in general to do with signs or symbols

definitions.text: to do with signs or symbols

indicators.note: the fringes of a word are its edges, its first and last letters
in places those letters inside the following word

blocks.note: the outside letters of occult
national means general, belonging to the whole country

explanation.surface: The fringe occult world, broadly concerned with signs and symbols.
explanation.definitionFit: Notation is a system of written signs, so notational means relating to such symbols.

clue.text: Comb for sale — two pounds off

indicators.note: off means removed, so those letters are taken away

blocks.note: for sale means available to sell
l is the abbreviation for a pound, twice

explanation.surface: A comb discounted by two pounds in a sale.
explanation.definitionFit: Tose is an old dialect word meaning to tease out or comb wool.

clue.text: Current affairs show casts a glad eye on big city in review

indicators.note: reviewing means looking back, so the whole string is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: to cast a glad eye is to leer
the Great Wen is an old nickname for London, so a wen is a big city

explanation.surface: A TV programme ogles a metropolis in its roundup.
explanation.walkthrough: A glad eye is an amorous look; the whole string LEERSWEN is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsreel was a short film of current events shown in cinemas, a current affairs show.
